newsitem.title: UK: UK's BDB in 200 mln stg digital deal with Castle.
newsitem.headline: UK's BDB in 200 mln stg digital deal with Castle.

text.p: British Digital Broadcasting (BDB) said on Monday it had selected Castle Transmission International (CTI) to provide the network to broadcast the 15 pay channels it will launch in the UK next year.

"This is an important step for BDB. Over the next 12 years, BDB expects to spend approximately 200 million stg on transmission as part of the advanced systems required to bring digitial terrestrial television (DTT) to people's homes," said BDB Director Nigel Walmsley.
BDB, owned by Carlton Communications Plc and Granada Group Plc, was recently awarded three key DTT licences.

CIT is a consortium including Houston-based Castle Tower Corporation and France Telecom unit Telediffusion de France. Earlier this year it acquired the BBC's domestic radio and television transmission business for 244 million stg.
BDB said the deal remained subject to contract but added it planned to begin test transmissions by the end of the year.

DTT, which will offer some 30 or so channels plus a limited range of interactive services, will be available via standard rooftop aerials rather than cable or satellite. Viewers will, however, need to buy a set-top decoder to receive the signals.
BDB plans to offer 12 channels in its basic subscription package plus three premium channels including programming from satellite broadcaster BSkyB Plc.
